p1_p6_canonical_strings.P1_receipt_completeness: Every step of a governed run leaves exactly one signed receipt; the log is append-only and gap-free -> an auditor can reconstruct the whole run.
p1_p6_canonical_strings.P2_gate_soundness: An action is allowed only if BOTH the policy check AND the kernel/doctrine check return ALLOW; a single failing check is absorbing and cannot be overridden downstream.
p1_p6_canonical_strings.P3_non_interference: HEADLINE: prompt-injection / poisoned retrieval provably cannot flip a DENY into an ALLOW. The untrusted context is recorded in the audit log yet quarantined from the decision (Goguen-Meseguer information-flow security).
p1_p6_canonical_strings.P4_replay_determinism: Re-running a recorded run from the same state reproduces a byte-identical receipt chain -> deterministic replay audit. Extends F1 from one step to the whole pipeline.
p1_p6_canonical_strings.P5_tamper_evidence: Any single-receipt payload tampering that doesn't recompute its hash makes chain re-verification reject -> forgery is detectable. Gated on the standard hash collision-resistance idealization (NIST FIPS 180-4).
p1_p6_canonical_strings.P6_monotone_auditability: An auditor who accepted the chain up to a point never has to retract that as the log grows -> streaming/incremental audit without re-checking history.
